content: The dispute arose from the division of a co-owned apartment and garage where neither party wished to buy out the other. The court examined Article 720 of the Civil Code, which governs the handling of "non-conveniently divisible" assets. The interpretive problem was how to proceed when a physical split of the property is technically impossible and neither party requests the assignment of the whole asset. The court applied the principle that if a property is indivisible and no party claims it in its entirety (with a conguaglio payment), the law mandates a judicial sale by auction. This ensures that the proceeds can be split equally (50% each), effectively satisfying the co-ownership rights of both former spouses.
